## Load packages

`pacman` loads the required packages and installs any that are missing. `here::i_am()` places
this notebook in the repository, so paths resolve from the repository root.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, dplyr, tibble, tidyr, readxl, writexl)
here::i_am("05_Mitochondria/01_build_mito_sets/a_script/01_build_mito_sets.qmd")
```

## Read MitoCarta and the protein map

MitoCarta 3.0 is the Broad Institute's inventory of human mitochondrial proteins, 1,136 genes. Its
workbook also lists 149 MitoPathways: curated functional groups such as "CI subunits" or "Fatty
acid oxidation". The file was downloaded on 2026-09-28 from
personal.broadinstitute.org/scalvo/MitoCarta3.0/.

`protein_map` comes from stage 03 and links each protein group to its gene symbol. `selected`
marks the one representative protein per symbol, the rows that `01_run_fgsea_and_fry` tests.

```{r read}
out <- here("05_Mitochondria", "01_build_mito_sets", "c_data")
mitocarta <- here("05_Mitochondria", "00_Input", "Human.MitoCarta3.0.xls")
protein_map <- read_excel(
  here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data", "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx"),
  "protein_gene_map"
)
head(protein_map, 3)
```

## Build the sets

The "C MitoPathways" sheet holds one row per pathway with its genes in one comma-separated cell.
`separate_longer_delim()` turns that into one row per pathway and gene. `col_types = "text"` stops
readxl guessing each column's type, which warns on this file. The pathways nest, so a parent such
as "Complex I" holds its children's genes too.

```{r pathways}
pathways <- read_excel(mitocarta, "C MitoPathways", col_types = "text") |>
  filter(!is.na(MitoPathway)) |>
  transmute(collection = "MitoPathways", set = MitoPathway, gene = Genes) |>
  separate_longer_delim(gene, ", ")
head(pathways, 3)
```

The full MitoCarta list is one more set, read from the "A Human MitoCarta3.0" sheet.

```{r all-mito}
all_mito <- tibble(
  collection = "MitoCarta", set = "MitoCarta",
  gene = read_excel(mitocarta, "A Human MitoCarta3.0", col_types = "text")$Symbol
)
```

A gene counts as measured when a representative protein carries its symbol.

```{r membership}
membership <- bind_rows(all_mito, pathways) |>
  mutate(measured = gene %in% protein_map$gene[protein_map$selected])
```

## Check the complexes

The complex readouts in `02_test_mito` are the pathways "CI subunits" to "CV subunits": the
structural subunits, mtDNA-encoded ones included. The parent pathways "Complex I" and so on also
hold assembly factors, which build a complex without tracking how much of it exists.

```{r complexes}
membership |>
  filter(set %in% c(paste(c("CI", "CII", "CIII", "CIV", "CV"), "subunits"), "Complex I")) |>
  summarise(listed = n(), measured = sum(measured), .by = set)
```

## Summary

Number of sets, genes listed and genes measured, per collection.

```{r summary}
membership |>
  summarise(
    sets = n_distinct(set), rows = n(), measured_rows = sum(measured),
    .by = collection
  )
```

## Save results

`01_build_mito_sets.xlsx` holds the `membership` sheet that `02_test_mito` and
`03_complex_subunits` read.

```{r write}
overview <- data.frame(
  sheet = "membership", rows = nrow(membership),
  description = "One row per set and gene, flagged if measured. 02_test_mito reads this sheet."
)
write_xlsx(
  list(overview = overview, membership = membership),
  file.path(out, "01_build_mito_sets.xlsx")
)
```
